finding.claim: The /fetch handler passes the unvalidated `target` query parameter straight to http.Get. An unauthenticated caller controls scheme, host and port, so they can reach internal services, loopback and cloud metadata endpoints (e.g. http://169.254.169.254/). The full response body is copied back to the caller, so this is not blind SSRF. Go's default client follows redirects, which adds a second route to internal hosts. Severity: HIGH.
finding.source: r.URL.Query().Get("target") at main.go:15 (HTTP query parameter on GET /fetch)
finding.sink: http.Get(target) at main.go:16; response streamed back via io.Copy(w, resp.Body) at main.go:22

trace.note: http.HandleFunc("/fetch", fetch) registers a public route
http.ListenAndServe(":8080", nil) binds all interfaces with no authentication middleware
target := r.URL.Query().Get("target") reads the attacker-controlled value
http.Get(target) issues the outbound request with no transformation or check in between
io.Copy(w, resp.Body) returns the fetched content to the attacker. Error text is also returned at main.go:18

finding.guards_checked: No allowlist, scheme check, hostname check or IP/CIDR block between source and sink. The allowed map at main.go:9 is used only by safeFetch, not by fetch. No CheckRedirect is set and http.Get uses the default client, which follows redirects. No auth middleware. Not a literal, env var or startup config. The user controls the whole URL, not just a path. Reproduction: curl 'http://HOST:8080/fetch?target=http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/' returns the metadata body, while a safe endpoint would return 403.

verdict.reason: main.go:15-16 passes the query param `target` directly to http.Get with no validation, and main.go:22 returns the body. The allowlist at main.go:27 guards only safeFetch, and the handler is public at main.go:41 and main.go:43 with no auth.
